title: Розыгрыш с запиской и Максим Галкин  (The Note Prank and Maxim Galkin)

segments.t: Holding a bouquet of flowers, Max arrives at the apartment address written in the note, expecting a secret rendezvous with his older admirer. When he steps inside the open door, Kostya, Senya, and Fedya jump out snapping photos and laughing that he is just like Maxim Galkin.
Мне передали вашу записку с адресом.
Да нет, вы в самый раз.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Hello there, Maxim.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'hello' and finishing on 'Maxim'. Kostya answers right away.
'Here I am!' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'and' and 'there you go' in a few short words.
'Wait, who told you my address?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'who' and finishing on 'address'.
'What are all of you doing here?' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'what' and 'you' in a few short words. Max answers right away.
Мне передали вашу записку с адресом.
'Someone passed me your note with the address.' The meaning hinges on 'for me' working together with 'address' in spoken Russian.
'I never passed you any note...' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'pass on' places the action in the masculine past tense.
'The door was unlocked.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'the door' before landing on 'opened'. Kostya answers right away.
'It looks like I came at a bad time.' The grammar packs 'alike' and 'time' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Да нет, вы в самый раз.
'Not at all, you arrived at the perfect moment.' Max brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'there is no' in a few short words.
'You should really just come to the restaurant instead.' Notice how Russian expresses 'you' and 'restaurant' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
'Alright then, Maxim.' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'Maxim' in spoken Russian.
'Maxim, man, you really are something!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Maxim' before landing on 'give'.
'You are regular Maxim Galkin.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'you' and finishing on 'Galkin'. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Мне передали вашу записку с адресом.
Да нет, вы в самый раз.
